title: Gandharan patrons expand Buddhist sacred complexes
summary: Gandhara saw increased patronage of Buddhist monasteries and sacred areas from the third to the mid-fifth century, alongside expanding sculptural production.

citations.locator: Paragraph beginning “From the third to the mid-fifth century” and discussion of stucco sculpture
citations.note: Supports the linked claims within the stated date and attribution limits.

claims.text: Gandhara saw increased patronage of Buddhist monasteries and sacred areas from the third to the mid-fifth century, alongside expanding sculptural production.
The boundaries translate the essay’s third-to-mid-fifth-century phase approximately; 201 and 450 are display coordinates, not documented turning points.
Stucco enabled rapid production of images that could be molded and painted. This phase followed earlier foundations and does not date Buddhism’s arrival.

review.corroboration: The Met’s phase discussion was inspected. An inconsistent date for a separate reliquary in the essay is outside this record’s claims.
